key_insight: R-DMesh adds a rectification stage that aligns a user-supplied static mesh to the starting pose of a reference video before applying dynamic mesh flow, preventing geometric distortion and enabling faithful video-guided 3D animation.
problem_solved: Addresses the pose misalignment dilemma: when a static mesh's initial pose doesn't match the video start frame, naive retargeting produces severe distortions or failed animations. R-DMesh makes video-guided animation robust to arbitrary initial mesh poses.
method: Rectification module: automatically align or optimize the static mesh's initial pose to match the video’s starting pose (pose transfer / pose optimization).
Dynamic mesh flow estimation: compute per-vertex temporal flow from the reference video to drive animation.
Geometry- and temporal-regularized deformation: apply the rectified flow with constraints (e.g., surface preservation, smoothness, temporal consistency) to avoid artifacts.
impact: Makes video-driven 3D animation practical and reliable for content creators and ML pipelines by removing the need for manual retargeting and reducing distortion, accelerating production of dynamic 3D assets.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison: same static mesh animated without rectification (distorted) vs. with R-DMesh (clean motion).
Pipeline diagram: video input → rectification module → dynamic mesh flow estimator → constrained deformation → animated mesh.
Flow visualization: per-vertex motion vectors or heatmap showing where rectification corrects large misalignments.
Quantitative charts: error or perceptual quality vs. baseline methods and an ablation chart showing impact of rectification and regularizers.
paper_title: R-DMesh: Video-Guided 3D Animation via Rectified Dynamic Mesh Flow
paper_authors: Zijie Wu, Lixin Xu, Puhua Jiang, Sicong Liu, Chunchao Guo
